title: 'Nobody wanted it to end': Seniors prom brings together long-term care residents, Brock University students

blocks.text: Hamilton

Their high school days might be in the rearview mirror, but residents of four long-term care homes in Ontario's Niagara region got to feel as if they were fresh-faced teenagers again, at a prom for seniors held in collaboration with Brock University students.
Intergenerational event at Linhaven an emotional one for residents

Their high school days might be in the rearview mirror, but residents of four long-term care homes in Ontario's Niagara region got to feel as if they were fresh-faced teenagers again, just like they were half a century ago or longer.
Residents at the special seniors prom even got to party with Brock University students at Linhaven long-term care home in St. Catharines.
The seniors prom had all the fixings of a high school one —balloons, food, music and dancing, minus the teenage angst and someone trying to spike the punch bowl.
When we started to plan this, talking to our residents, a lot of them were saying they never attended their proms. It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.- Heather Wild, Linhaven program manager
The intergenerational event was a huge hit, so much so that the afternoon prom went longer than it was supposed to.
"Nobody wanted it to end," said Heather Wild, program manager at Linhaven.

Residents from the three other long-term care homes operated by Niagara's regional government — Rapelje Lodge in Welland, Northland Pointe in Port Colborne and Woodlands of Sunset on the border of Welland and Pelham — were bused to the prom.
Prom was part of Brock Cares outreach

In all, more than 60 residents, some of family members and 25 Brock students were at the Linhaven prom, among a number of events that the university students volunteered to go to across Niagara on Saturday as part of the Brock Cares community outreach program.
For Emily Poole, a third-year concurrent education student, it was her third year as a Brock Cares volunteer. When she heard about the seniors prom, she couldn't miss it.
"The event was full of energy. The turnout was amazing."
Poole said it was heart-warming to see the residents get dressed up in formal attire with prom-like dresses and suits. There was even someone on site doing hair and makeup.
Wild said it was the first such event held in collaboration with Brock Cares, plus a first for many of the long-term care residents.
"When we started to plan this, talking to our residents, a lot of them were saying they never attended their proms," she said. "It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity."
Poole volunteered in the photo booth, taking residents' photos with "silly" props.
"It was great to see their personalities shine and their excitement grow," she said, calling it "incredibly rewarding."

With a backdrop of white, gold and black balloons, and a disco ball twinkling overhead, residents satiated their sweet tooth with treats such as brownies, and custard with Linhaven Prom 2026 written with powdered chocolate on the creamy treat.
The students handed a rose to each woman.

blocks.text: Wild said the dance floor was hopping, first with some oldies but goodies, and then with residents' requests to the DJ.
"Some wedding songs were requested," she said. "That made it very special because it was very personal to the residents.
"There were residents and some family members who were very emotional. There were some tears."
Brock students are scheduled to return to Linhaven in the fall to help with Halloween and Thanksgiving events, Wild said.
